prompt.context_jp: ハナ___たった独りで見知らぬ街の路地を歩いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナ___たった独りで見知らぬ街の路地を歩いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits as this chapter establishes Hana as its ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: The chapter opens by framing Hana as the known, continuing topic the narration will track — classic は territory.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Hana as fresh, newsworthy information (as if answering 'who was walking?'), but she is already the story's protagonist.

contrast_examples.jp: ハナは歩いていた。
contrast_examples.en: As for Hana, she was walking. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: ハナが歩いていた。
contrast_examples.en: It was Hana who was walking. (new/identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 路地の角で、見知らぬ男の手___ハナの鞄を掠め取った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 見知らぬ男の手___ハナの鞄を掠め取った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this sudden event.

feedback.correct_en: An unfamiliar hand appears for the first time — new, event-reporting information, which calls for が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the hand as an already-known topic, but it bursts into the scene unannounced.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に雨が降ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly rain started falling. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: その雨はすぐにやんだ。
contrast_examples.en: That rain soon stopped. (now a topic)

prompt.context_jp: 恐怖と怒り___一対の翼のように背を押した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 恐怖と怒り___一対の翼のように背を押した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the newly-named feelings driving her body?

feedback.correct_en: Fear and anger are introduced here as the specific forces propelling her — fresh information, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn these emotions into a general topic ('as for fear and anger…'), which doesn't match this surge-of-action moment.

contrast_examples.jp: 涙が止まらなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Tears wouldn't stop. (new, situational)

contrast_examples.jp: 涙は我慢した。
contrast_examples.en: The tears, I held back. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: 路地は幾つにも枝分かれし、男の姿___すぐに人波の中へ紛れていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 男の姿___すぐに人波の中へ紛れていった。
prompt.prompt_en: The thief has already been introduced. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The man's figure is now a known referent that the narrator comments about ('as for his figure, it quickly vanished'). は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce him as new information, but we have been chasing him for several sentences already.

contrast_examples.jp: その人の姿はもう見えなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That person's figure was no longer visible. (known)

contrast_examples.jp: 突然ある男の姿が現れた。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly a man's figure appeared. (new)

prompt.context_jp: 走り疲れて立ち止まったハナの前に、一人の見知らぬ男___息を切らして駆け寄ってくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一人の見知らぬ男___息を切らして駆け寄ってくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for a brand-new character entering the scene?

feedback.correct_en: A new stranger appears — the first time he enters the story. New-information が is standard here, and 一人の見知らぬ男 explicitly flags newness.
feedback.incorrect_en: は presumes the man is already known as a topic, but he has not been introduced yet.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人の男が走ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: A man came running up. (introducing)

contrast_examples.jp: その男は親切だった。
contrast_examples.en: That man was kind. (now a topic)

prompt.context_jp: 盗まれた鞄には確かに大事な資料も入っていたが、幸い財布とパスポート___上着の内側にあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 幸い財布とパスポート___上着の内側にあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets wallet/passport off against the lost documents.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts the stolen documents with items that were safe. は gives that contrastive focus ('as for the wallet and passport, those were in her jacket').
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely report who/what was in the pocket neutrally, losing the 'luckily, these on the other hand…' nuance the narration builds.

contrast_examples.jp: 鞄は盗まれたが、財布は無事だった。
contrast_examples.en: The bag was stolen, but the wallet was safe. (contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: 財布が見つかった。
contrast_examples.en: The wallet was found. (reporting new fact)

prompt.context_jp: 縋るような眼差しに、男___少しの間だけ黙って写真を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 男___少しの間だけ黙って写真を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The helpful stranger has already been established. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 'The man' refers back to the known helper. The narration continues his thread as topic, so は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight him as newly introduced or in exhaustive contrast with others, neither of which matches this quiet moment.

contrast_examples.jp: 男は黙って写真を見た。
contrast_examples.en: The man silently looked at the photo. (ongoing topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 男が黙って写真を見た。
contrast_examples.en: A man silently looked at the photo. (new/identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 舗装のない道は雨のあとらしく湿り、靴底に赤い土___絡んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 靴底に赤い土___絡んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this sensory detail added to the scene?

feedback.correct_en: The red soil is newly noticed descriptive detail — the kind of 'look what's happening' observation が introduces.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would single out 'red soil' as a topic being contrasted with something else, which the sentence isn't doing.

contrast_examples.jp: 服にほこりがついていた。
contrast_examples.en: Dust was clinging to the clothes. (descriptive new)

contrast_examples.jp: 服はほこりだらけだった。
contrast_examples.en: The clothes were covered in dust. (topic comment)

prompt.context_jp: 街の外れへ向かうほど、行き交う人の数___減り、家々の間隔も広くなっていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 行き交う人の数___減り、家々の間隔も広くなっていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up this paired contrast with 家々の間隔も…?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence pairs 'the number of people' with 'the spacing of houses' using は…も to list parallel changes. は frames the first element of that contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the first clause an event report, breaking the parallel 'A は…, B も…' pattern that the narration sets up.

contrast_examples.jp: 空は青く、海も青い。
contrast_examples.en: The sky is blue, and the sea is also blue. (parallel topics)

contrast_examples.jp: 空が晴れた。
contrast_examples.en: The sky cleared. (reporting an event)

prompt.context_jp: 気付けばハナ___、崩れかけた煉瓦塀に挟まれた薄暗い袋小路にひとり立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気付けばハナ___、…薄暗い袋小路にひとり立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that keeps Hana as the narrative topic.

feedback.correct_en: The narration continues tracking Hana as its topic throughout the chapter. は keeps that frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight Hana as newly identified ('it was Hana who was standing there'), but she is the known POV character.

contrast_examples.jp: ハナはそこに立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Hana was standing there. (topic frame)

contrast_examples.jp: そこにハナが立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: There stood Hana. (presenting her)

prompt.context_jp: 塀の陰から、複数の男たち___ゆっくりと姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 複数の男たち___ゆっくりと姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for men suddenly emerging from behind the wall?

feedback.correct_en: The men appear for the first time — a dramatic reveal. が introduces new entities into the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the men as already-topical, but this is the moment the threat is unveiled.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアの向こうから子供たちが出てきた。
contrast_examples.en: Children came out from beyond the door. (new)

contrast_examples.jp: その子供たちは笑っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Those children were laughing. (known)

prompt.context_jp: 逃げ道___塞がれ、退路___路地の奥だけである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 逃げ道___塞がれ、退路___路地の奥だけである。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle used for both blanks in this paired description.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence lays out two topic-comment statements in parallel: 'the escape route — blocked; the retreat path — only deeper in.' は frames each as topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as surprised discovery rather than the measured, almost resigned stock-taking the narration gives.

contrast_examples.jp: 右は壁、左は崖だった。
contrast_examples.en: To the right, a wall; to the left, a cliff. (parallel topics)

contrast_examples.jp: 右に壁があった。
contrast_examples.en: There was a wall on the right. (reporting)

prompt.context_jp: 振り下ろされた腕を、影のように駆け付けた大きな体___受け止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 影のように駆け付けた大きな体___受け止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the sudden rescuer bursting into frame?

feedback.correct_en: Someone unidentified crashes in to save Hana — classic 'who did this?' moment answered by が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would need the 'large body' to already be known as a topic, but his identity is held back for drama.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰かが助けてくれた。
contrast_examples.en: Someone saved me. (identifying new agent)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はいつも助けてくれる。
contrast_examples.en: He always helps me. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 静けさが戻った路地に、壮亮の荒い呼吸だけ___残される。
prompt.prompt_jp: 壮亮の荒い呼吸だけ___残される。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle paired with だけ for an exhaustive 'only this remains' reading.

feedback.correct_en: だけが pinpoints the sole thing filling the silence — exhaustive identification, which selects が.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは is possible in some contexts (contrastive 'at least this'), but here the narration is spotlighting the single sound that remains, which calls for が.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけが知っている。
contrast_examples.en: Only he knows (sole knower).

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけは知らなかった。
contrast_examples.en: He alone didn't know (contrastive).

prompt.context_jp: 壮亮___自分の傷よりも、その傷を先に見つけて眉をひそめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 壮亮___自分の傷よりも、その傷を先に見つけて眉をひそめた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames Sōryō's priorities against his own wound.

feedback.correct_en: Sōryō is the known character here, and the sentence makes a comment about his priorities (他人の傷を先に…). は fits a topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly identify who did the frowning, but Sōryō's actions have been in focus for several lines already.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は自分より人を優先する。
contrast_examples.en: He puts others before himself. (topic comment)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が気付いた。
contrast_examples.en: He was the one who noticed. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 傾いた夕陽___二人の影を長く伸ばしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 傾いた夕陽___二人の影を長く伸ばしている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this scene-setting descriptive line?

feedback.correct_en: A one-shot descriptive sentence introducing the atmospheric detail of the evening sun. が presents the sun as fresh scenic information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the sun as an ongoing topic to be commented on, but this is a standalone painterly image.

contrast_examples.jp: 雪が静かに降っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Snow was quietly falling. (scenic reporting)

contrast_examples.jp: 雪は三日間降り続いた。
contrast_examples.en: The snow (as a topic) kept falling for three days.

prompt.context_jp: 肩で息をする彼と、うつむいたままのハナの間に、しばしの沈黙___落ちる。
prompt.prompt_jp: しばしの沈黙___落ちる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for a silence that newly settles between them?

feedback.correct_en: The silence 'falls' between them as a fresh event — new information marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require 'silence' to be an already-topical referent, but it is being presented just now.

contrast_examples.jp: 気まずい沈黙が流れた。
contrast_examples.en: An awkward silence flowed. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: その沈黙は長かった。
contrast_examples.en: That silence was long. (now topic)

prompt.context_jp: 人の視線が___な彼女にとって、異国の雑踏そのものが試練のようなものだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の視線が___な彼女にとって…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that captures Hana's scopophobia.

feedback.correct_en: 苦手 collocates with 視線 to mean 'bad at handling / uncomfortable with' others' gazes — exactly Hana's condition.
feedback.incorrect_en: 得意/上手 mean 'good at,' which is the opposite feeling. 下手 is about skill at an activity, not emotional discomfort with being looked at.

contrast_examples.jp: 人前が苦手だ。
contrast_examples.en: I'm uncomfortable in front of people.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理が下手だ。
contrast_examples.en: I'm bad at cooking. (skill, not emotion)

prompt.context_jp: 逃がしてはいけない、その___だけが体を動かしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 逃がしてはいけない、その___だけが体を動かしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits the single-minded drive carrying her forward?

feedback.correct_en: 一心 = a single-minded intent / all-consuming focus, the exact shade needed for 'that one thought alone drove my body.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 一面 (one aspect/side), 一度 (once), and 一方 (on the other hand / one side) don't convey the obsessive mental drive.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けたい一心で走った。
contrast_examples.en: I ran, moved by the single wish to help.

contrast_examples.jp: 一度だけ試した。
contrast_examples.en: I tried just once.

prompt.context_jp: ハナは想像していた農場とは違うその佇まいに、思わず息を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 思わず息を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb forms the idiom for being stunned into holding one's breath?

feedback.correct_en: 息を呑む is the set idiom for gasping/being taken aback in awe or shock — fits her reaction to the unexpected building.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を吸う/吐く are literal 'inhale/exhale'; 息を切らす means to be out of breath. None carry the 'struck speechless' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 美しさに息を呑んだ。
contrast_examples.en: I gasped at the beauty.

contrast_examples.jp: 走って息を切らした。
contrast_examples.en: I ran and got out of breath.

prompt.context_jp: 戸口で見送ってくれた老いた医者に、ハナは深く頭を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナは深く頭を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb forms the standard 'bow one's head' collocation?

feedback.correct_en: 頭を下げる is the fixed phrase for bowing in gratitude or respect, matching the context of thanking the doctor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 頭を落とす suggests dejection; 頭を曲げる isn't a natural idiom; 頭を振る means to shake one's head 'no.'

contrast_examples.jp: 深く頭を下げた。
contrast_examples.en: She bowed deeply.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は頭を振って断った。
contrast_examples.en: He shook his head and declined.

prompt.context_jp: 冗談めかしたその仕草の奥に、確かな___の色があった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 冗談めかしたその仕草の奥に、確かな___の色があった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures Sōryō's inner resolve behind the joking bow?

feedback.correct_en: 覚悟 (resolve / preparedness to accept consequences) matches the gravity of asking Hana to represent the shop.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自慢 (pride/boasting), 興味 (interest), and 緊張 (nervousness) don't convey the determined commitment under the jokey tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 覚悟の色が目に浮かぶ。
contrast_examples.en: A look of resolve shows in his eyes.

contrast_examples.jp: 緊張の色が見えた。
contrast_examples.en: A look of nervousness was visible.

prompt.context_jp: 荒事は明らかに苦手そうな身のこなしだったが、それでもハナを___位置から一歩も退かなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: それでもハナを___位置から一歩も退かなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'protecting / shielding' Hana?

feedback.correct_en: 庇う means to shield / cover for someone — exactly Sōryō's stance between Hana and the attackers.
feedback.incorrect_en: 追う (chase), 避ける (avoid), 責める (blame) don't fit a protective stance.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供を庇って立った。
contrast_examples.en: He stood shielding the child.

contrast_examples.jp: 責任を避ける。
contrast_examples.en: To dodge responsibility.

prompt.context_jp: ちょっと問題がある傷んだ実が 逆に神からの ___だったなんて それこそが奇跡でした
prompt.prompt_jp: 逆に神からの ___だった
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'a ___ from God' — a blessing, not a trial?

feedback.correct_en: 贈り物 (gift) matches 'reversed into a blessing' — the damaged fruit turned out to be a godsend.
feedback.incorrect_en: 試練/罰/命令 (trial/punishment/order) would be negative or neutral; the sentence hinges on the fruit being an unexpected blessing.

contrast_examples.jp: 神からの贈り物だった。
contrast_examples.en: It was a gift from God.

contrast_examples.jp: それは試練だった。
contrast_examples.en: That was a trial.

prompt.context_jp: 強張っていたハナの肩も、温かい匂いに少しずつ___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 強張っていたハナの肩も、温かい匂いに少しずつ___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb matches tense shoulders being eased by a warm scent?

feedback.correct_en: ほどける literally 'come untied' and figuratively applies to tension unknotting — the natural image for tense shoulders relaxing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊れる (break), 固まる (stiffen — the opposite!), 消える (disappear — shoulders don't vanish) all miss the 'tension loosens' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 緊張がほどけた。
contrast_examples.en: The tension loosened.

contrast_examples.jp: 表情が固まった。
contrast_examples.en: Her expression stiffened.

prompt.context_jp: Opening line introducing Hana walking the alley.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as the chapter's opening sentence?

choices.text: ハナはたった独りで見知らぬ街の路地を歩いていた。
ハナがたった独りで見知らぬ街の路地を歩いていた。

feedback.correct_en: An opening narrative line that frames the protagonist and her situation typically uses は to set the topic. The source text uses は for this reason.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read like a report answering 'who was walking?' — fine mid-scene, but jarring as a chapter-opening frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 昔むかし、ある村におじいさんが住んでいました。
contrast_examples.en: Long ago, there lived an old man in a village. (new, presentational)

contrast_examples.jp: おじいさんは山へ柴刈りに行きました。
contrast_examples.en: The old man went to the mountain. (now topic)

prompt.context_jp: Just after Hana realizes she's trapped in the alley.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for the moment attackers emerge?

choices.text: 塀の陰から、複数の男たちがゆっくりと姿を現した。
塀の陰から、複数の男たちはゆっくりと姿を現した。

feedback.correct_en: A sudden reveal of previously-unknown figures calls for が. The source uses が because this is the first appearance of the attackers.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the men were already an established topic ('as for those men, they emerged slowly'), which contradicts the dramatic reveal.

contrast_examples.jp: 物陰から猫が飛び出した。
contrast_examples.en: A cat leapt out from the shadow. (new)

contrast_examples.jp: その猫はうちで飼っている。
contrast_examples.en: That cat (as topic) we keep at home.

prompt.context_jp: Hana scolding Sōryō for getting hurt.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for Hana's exasperated worry?

choices.text: かなり心配したじゃないですか！
かなり心配しましたじゃないですか！

feedback.correct_en: じゃないですか attaches to the plain past 心配した, not to the polite past. The source uses 心配したじゃないですか to express 'I was really worried, you know!'
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配しましたじゃないですか mixes polite ます-form with the ~じゃない tag ending, which is ungrammatical in standard Japanese.

contrast_examples.jp: 言ったじゃないですか。
contrast_examples.en: I told you, didn't I!

contrast_examples.jp: ✗ 言いましたじゃないですか。
contrast_examples.en: (unnatural mix of registers)

prompt.context_jp: After the attackers flee, in the quiet alley.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for 'only his breathing remained'?

choices.text: 壮亮の荒い呼吸だけが残される。
壮亮の荒い呼吸だけは残される。

feedback.correct_en: 'Only X remains / is left' as a sole-surviving element uses だけが. The source line pinpoints his breathing as the one sound filling the silence.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは adds a 'at least X' contrastive flavor ('X alone was spared'), which doesn't match the stillness/aftermath image here.

contrast_examples.jp: 灯りだけがついていた。
contrast_examples.en: Only the light was on. (sole)

contrast_examples.jp: それだけは譲れない。
contrast_examples.en: That alone I won't yield (contrastive).

prompt.context_jp: Hana declaring her reason for entering the competition.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is more natural for 'it's for myself, not for anyone else'?

choices.text: 誰かのためじゃなく、自分のためです。
誰かのためじゃない、自分のためにです。

feedback.correct_en: The parallel 〜のためじゃなく、〜のためです is the natural, balanced phrasing used in the source line. The です cleanly closes 自分のため.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自分のためにです sounds awkward because に before です isn't needed — ため as a noun already takes です directly.

contrast_examples.jp: お金のためじゃなく、夢のためです。
contrast_examples.en: It's not for money — it's for a dream.

contrast_examples.jp: ✗ 夢のためにです。
contrast_examples.en: (unnatural; ため + に + です clashes)
